title: Kissy Face Emoji 😘 Meaning: Love, Thanks or Flirting?
description: 😘 blows a kiss with a little red heart. It can say “love you,” “thanks, you're a star,” or something flirtier. Here's how to read it by who sent it.
summary: The 😘 face blowing a kiss winks and sends a small red heart from its lips. It means affection: a kiss goodbye, “love you,” or warm thanks. Partners use it romantically, friends and family use it platonically, and from someone new it often counts as flirting.
meaning: Of all the kissing faces, this is the only one with a heart, and that heart makes it the most popular by a wide margin. It turns a kiss into a message with a destination. The classic use is a sign-off between people who are close: “night 😘,” “drive safe 😘.” It stands in for the kiss you would give in person or the “mwah” at the end of a phone call.

It doubles as a thank-you. When a friend covers your shift or a sister sends the recipe you asked for, “you're the best 😘” expresses gratitude with affection. Many people, especially women texting friends, use it this way all day without any romantic thought. In some families it ends nearly every message.

Romantic and flirtatious uses are just as established. Between partners it is everyday shorthand for love. From someone you are getting to know, a 😘 raises the temperature: it is more forward than a smile and gentler than outright innuendo. The wink built into the face adds a teasing note that pure affection emojis do not have.

It can be cheeky as well. After a sassy remark, 😘 works like blowing a kiss while walking away: “guess you'll have to try harder next time 😘.” There the meaning is playful triumph, even mild sarcasm. The same sweetness that makes it loving makes it a good vehicle for a friendly taunt.

contexts.label: In a relationship
contexts.body: A daily staple. It closes good-morning and goodnight texts, accompanies “miss you,” and answers small favors. Couples often settle into a pattern, and a sudden absence of the usual 😘 can be noticed more than its presence. It is affectionate and a little playful, less solemn than a red heart.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: Worth noticing. If you are not yet close, a kiss emoji is a deliberate step past friendliness, especially at the end of a late message or after a compliment. Some people do send it to everyone, so compare. Sent to you alone, it is a reasonable sign of interest.

contexts.label: With friends and family
contexts.body: Fully platonic and very common. Mothers, aunts, and close friends use it as a warm goodbye or thanks. Among female friends it is often paired with “babe” or “love.” Cultural habits differ: in communities where cheek kisses are a normal greeting, 😘 is used more freely.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: Generally best avoided. Even where colleagues are friendly, a kiss can be misread or make someone uncomfortable. Exceptions exist between real friends who happen to work together. For thanks in a professional setting, 🙏 or 😊 delivers the warmth without the intimacy.

examples.text: Thanks for picking up the kids, you're a lifesaver 😘
examples.meaning: Grateful affection toward a partner or relative.

examples.text: Can't wait to see you Friday 😘
Love you, call me when you land 😘

examples.meaning: A cheeky, teasing sign-off after winning.
Warm wishes to a close friend or partner.

combos.meaning: Love and a kiss; an openly romantic or deeply affectionate sign-off.
Lots of kisses, often from family or an enthusiastic partner.
Flirting: a tease followed by a kiss.

confusedWith.difference: 😗 has puckered lips, open eyes, and no heart. It is a neutral peck and is often used for whistling or acting casual. 😘 winks and blows a heart, making it clearly affectionate and the default for sending a kiss.
😚 closes its eyes and blushes while kissing, with no heart. It feels tender and bashful, like a real kiss. 😘 is more outgoing and playful: a kiss blown across the room, not one delivered up close.
💋 is a lipstick print. It reads as glamorous, sassy, or sensual and is common in beauty content and sign-offs. 😘 is warmer and more personal, since it shows a face making the gesture.

avoid: Don't send it to colleagues, clients, or acquaintances unless you already have that kind of friendship.
Avoid it with someone whose romantic interest you do not return, because it can be taken as encouragement.
Skip the cheeky use after a real argument, where it will look dismissive.
design: A yellow face with one eye winking, lips puckered, and a small red heart floating beside the mouth. The heart is the key element and appears on every platform. Which eye winks and exactly where the heart sits vary slightly. Apple, Google, Samsung, and Microsoft all depict the same blown-kiss gesture.

faqs.q: Does 😘 mean someone likes me romantically?
faqs.a: It might. Between people who are not already close, it usually signals flirtation. But many people send it to friends and family as a habit. Whether they send it to others is the most useful clue.

faqs.q: What does 😘 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: Men generally use it less casually than women, so from a guy who is not a relative it often indicates romantic or flirtatious interest. From a partner it is routine affection. Some men do use it jokingly with friends.

faqs.q: What does 😘 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: Possibly affection, possibly just friendliness. Plenty of women use it as a standard thank-you or goodbye with friends. If she sends it specifically to you, with compliments or plans to meet, it leans toward flirting.

faqs.q: Is 😘 okay to send to friends?
faqs.a: Yes, if that suits your friendship. Many friend groups use it constantly. If you are unsure how it will be received, particularly with a friend of the gender you are attracted to, a heart in a non-red color or 🫶 is less ambiguous.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 😘 and 😚?
faqs.a: 😘 winks and blows a heart; it is lively and can be flirtatious. 😚 has closed eyes and a blush; it is softer and more intimate. 😘 is far more widely used.
